messages:
From: Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@acme-corp.com>

Subject: SIG: encryption questions (at-rest / in-transit) + evidence request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Acme's SIG review we'd like more detail on Redwood's encryption posture specifically around:

- Encryption in transit (TLS versions, mutual TLS for private deployments, cipher suites)
- Encryption at rest (envelope encryption, where keys are stored, who controls root keys)
- KMS / HSM usage (vendor, HSM attestation, separation of duties)
- Key rotation (frequency, rotation windows, evidence for rotations in the last 12 months)

Can you provide a concise summary for each item above and attach any evidence we can include in the SIG packet (architecture diagram, rotation logs, HSM attestation, runbook excerpt)? If anything is customer-configurable (BYOK, customer-managed keys), please call that out.

Target for our internal reviewers: EOD next Tuesday if possible. Please cc your security contact.

Thanks,
Amanda
Amanda Liu
Security Program Manager, Acme Corp
amanda.liu@acme-corp.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: encryption questions (at-rest / in-transit) + evidence request

Amanda,

Appreciate the clear list — forwarding to our security and infra leads and pulling together the evidence. High-level answers below; attaching the artifacts you requested and we can follow with additional detail if you want deeper technical sections.

Summary (short):
- In transit: All public endpoints use TLS 1.3. Private deployments (VPC/private control plane) support mTLS for mutual auth between customer proxies and our runtime. Cipher suites are modern (AES-GCM / CHACHA20 where supported).
- At rest: We use envelope encryption. Data keys (DEKs) are generated per-tenant and encrypted with a Key Encryption Key (KEK) stored in an HSM-backed KMS.
- KMS/HSM: Root KEKs are stored in AWS CloudHSM clusters for hosted/dedicated; Private on-prem options support customer-supplied HSMs (BYOK). HSM attestation pack attached.
- Rotation: Data keys are rotated automatically per policy (default monthly for DEKs); KEKs are rotated on a scheduled cadence (default annual) or on-demand for incidents. We have rotation logs for the last 12 months attached.

Attachments included: kms-architecture-diagram-2028.pdf; key-rotation-log-2027-2028.csv; hsm-attestation-2027.pdf

I'll CC Laura (Security) and Hiro (Infra) on the next message for more granular technical items and the runbook excerpt.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SIG: encryption questions (at-rest / in-transit) + evidence request

Amanda,

Looping in Laura (Head of Security) and Hiro (Infra) — see answers below and a short runbook excerpt attached. We also dropped a SOC 2 reference link in the related links field.

Detailed answers:
- KEK rotation window: KEK rotations are designed to be non-disruptive using dual-wrapping and key provenance checks. Typical maintenance window: 15–45 minutes for the rotation operation across shards; traffic is not paused, but there is a brief increase in KMS API calls while new ciphertexts are written. We schedule rotations during low-traffic windows by default and can provide blackout windows if Acme requires.

- Who performs the rotation: Rotations are executed by an automated orchestration service that runs in our control plane and is kicked off by a scheduled job. The actual rewrapping operation uses HSM-backed keys and is authorized with a multi-step approval process for KEK rotation (automation + human approval for root KEK rotations). For KEK root rotations we perform a key ceremony; runbook excerpt attached.

- Tenant isolation and BYOK: For Dedicated and Private deployments, KEKs are single-tenant by default. BYOK is supported: customers can import key material into a customer-managed HSM (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM) and Red­wood does not export customer key material once imported. We provide HSM attestation and audit logs as evidence of non-export.

- TLS cipher suites: Primary TLS 1.3 suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 (where supported). For older mutual-TLS connections we support TLS 1.2 with ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256.

- SOC 2: Our SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; link is listed in related links and we can initiate access with Acme's compliance mailbox. Controls relevant to KMS/HSM, rotation, and access logging are covered under CC6 and CC7 in the report.

Attachments in this message: key-rotation-runbook-brief.md (excerpt), kms-architecture-diagram-2028.pdf (repeat), key-rotation-log-2027-2028.csv (repeat), hsm-attestation-2027.pdf (repeat).

If you'd like, Laura can provide a short notarized statement for your SIG packet confirming key custody practices and attestation sources — Laura, any objections?

Thanks,
Karthik
